verdict: Comcast revenue fell 6.1% to $29.3B against a year-ago quarter boosted by big one-off items — flat on a like-for-like basis — as Peacock turned profitable again and broadband kept shrinking slowly.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: -6.1% YoY; +0.5% on a pro forma like-for-like basis

kpis.label: Peacock
kpis.note: revenue, with $261M of Adjusted EBITDA — its second straight profitable quarter

segments.name: Connectivity & Platforms
segments.note: Broadband, wireless, video and business services — Residential brought in $17,018M (-3.5%, as broadband and video customers keep drifting away) and Business Services $2,645M (+2.7%).

segments.name: Content & Experiences
segments.note: Media $5,359M (+13%, including Peacock and $224M of FIFA World Cup revenue), Studios $2,967M (-1.1%, though Universal passed $5B at the global box office) and Theme Parks $2,597M (-4.4%), less $400M of eliminations between them.

segments.name: Corporate, other & eliminations
segments.note: Corporate revenue of $341M (overhead businesses, regional sports networks, the Philadelphia Flyers) minus $1,242M of eliminations — sales between Comcast's own segments that are removed so they are not counted twice, with a $1M rounding difference.

opex.name: Other operating & administrative
opex.note: Running the networks, parks and studios day to day — the biggest running-cost line in Comcast's accounts.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the cable network, equipment and buildings. Comcast reports depreciation inside operating expenses; it is shown here as its own line so the page ties to reported operating income.

opex.name: Marketing & promotion
opex.note: Advertising Xfinity, Peacock, films and parks.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of acquired intangible assets — down from $1,666M a year ago.

otherDetail: A net $874M cost below operating profit: $962M of interest expense, partly offset by $88M of investment and other income (including $129M of earnings from businesses Comcast part-owns, less a $46M loss on equity securities).
footerNote: Programming and production costs ($7,515M) are shown as the cost of revenue — the direct cost of the content and networks Comcast sells; all other reported cost lines are operating expenses, so the page ties exactly to reported operating income of $5,320M. The flow uses total net income of $3,362M; after an $87M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to Comcast was $3,448M ($0.97 per diluted share). Pro forma figures adjust last year for the Versant separation (completed Jan 2, 2026) and the sale of Sky Germany (May 31, 2026).
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The headline fall is mostly last year's story
takeaways.text: Reported revenue fell 6.1%, but last year's quarter is not comparable — Versant has been separated and Sky Germany sold. On Comcast's pro forma basis, revenue rose 0.5% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 0.8%.

takeaways.title: Peacock is profitable — again
takeaways.text: Peacock made $261M of Adjusted EBITDA on $1.8B of revenue, its second straight profitable quarter, helped by the FIFA World Cup. A year ago it lost $217M. Media Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $769M.

takeaways.title: The cable core keeps eroding
takeaways.text: Residential Connectivity revenue fell 3.5% as broadband and video shrink; wireless is the offset — 368,000 lines added in the quarter, 10.6 million in total — and Business Services grew 2.7%.

oneTimers: GAAP EPS of $0.97 vs adjusted EPS of $1.07: the adjusted figures strip out items Comcast lists in its reconciliation, including amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and other gains and losses it does not count as operating performance.
